paragraphs.text: Now after two days was [the feast of] the passover and the unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him with subtlety, and kill him:
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὰ ἄζυμα μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας. καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς πῶς αὐτὸν ἐν δόλῳ κρατήσαντες ἀποκτείνωσιν,
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de to pascha kai ta azyma meta dyo hēmeras. kai ezētoun hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis pōs auton en dolō kratēsantes apokteinōsin,

paragraphs.text: for they said, Not during the feast, lest haply there shall be a tumult of the people.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγον γάρ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, μήποτε ἔσται θόρυβος τοῦ λαοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: elegon gar· Mē en tē heortē, mēpote estai thorybos tou laou.

paragraphs.text: And while he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster cruse of ointment of pure nard very costly; [and] she brake the cruse, and poured it over his head.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὄντος αὐτοῦ ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ κατακειμένου αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτελοῦς· συντρίψασα τὴν ἀλάβαστρον κατέχεεν αὐτοῦ τῆς κεφαλῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ontos autou en Bēthania en tē oikia Simōnos tou leprou katakeimenou autou ēlthen gynē echousa alabastron myrou nardou pistikēs polytelous· syntripsasa tēn alabastron katecheen autou tēs kephalēs.

paragraphs.text: But there were some that had indignation among themselves, [saying], To what purpose hath this waste of the ointment been made?
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἀγανακτοῦντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη τοῦ μύρου γέγονεν;
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de tines aganaktountes pros heautous· Eis ti hē apōleia hautē tou myrou gegonen;

paragraphs.text: For this ointment might have been sold for above three hundred shillings, and given to the poor. And they murmured against her.
paragraphs.original: ἠδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο τὸ μύρον πραθῆναι ἐπάνω δηναρίων τριακοσίων καὶ δοθῆναι τοῖς πτωχοῖς· καὶ ἐνεβριμῶντο αὐτῇ.
paragraphs.translit: ēdynato gar touto to myron prathēnai epanō dēnariōn triakosiōn kai dothēnai tois ptōchois· kai enebrimōnto autē.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus said, Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄφετε αὐτήν· τί αὐτῇ κόπους παρέχετε; καλὸν ἔργον ἠργάσατο ἐν ἐμοί·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen· Aphete autēn· ti autē kopous parechete; kalon ergon ērgasato en emoi·

paragraphs.text: For ye have the poor always with you, and whensoever ye will ye can do them good: but me ye have not always.
paragraphs.original: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν, καὶ ὅταν θέλητε δύνασθε αὐτοῖς εὖ ποιῆσαι, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·
paragraphs.translit: pantote gar tous ptōchous echete methʼ heautōn, kai hotan thelēte dynasthe autois eu poiēsai, eme de ou pantote echete·

paragraphs.text: She hath done what she could; she hath anointed my body beforehand for the burying.
paragraphs.original: ὃ ἔσχεν ἐποίησεν, προέλαβεν μυρίσαι τὸ σῶμά μου εἰς τὸν ἐνταφιασμόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho eschen epoiēsen, proelaben myrisai to sōma mou eis ton entaphiasmon.

paragraphs.text: And verily I say unto you, Wheresoever the gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, that also which this woman hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη λαληθήσεται εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: amēn de legō hymin, hopou ean kērychthē to euangelion eis holon ton kosmon, kai ho epoiēsen hautē lalēthēsetai eis mnēmosynon autēs.

paragraphs.text: And Judas Iscariot, he that was one of the twelve, went away unto the chief priests, that he might deliver him unto them.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριὼθ ὁ εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδοῖ αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai Ioudas Iskariōth ho heis tōn dōdeka apēlthen pros tous archiereis hina auton paradoi autois.

paragraphs.text: And they, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently deliver him [unto them].
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐχάρησαν καὶ ἐπηγγείλαντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι. καὶ ἐζήτει πῶς αὐτὸν εὐκαίρως παραδοῖ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de akousantes echarēsan kai epēngeilanto autō argyrion dounai. kai ezētei pōs auton eukairōs paradoi.

paragraphs.text: And on the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the passover, his disciples say unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and make ready that thou mayest eat the passover?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν ἀζύμων, ὅτε τὸ πάσχα ἔθυον, λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Ποῦ θέλεις ἀπελθόντες ἑτοιμάσωμεν ἵνα φάγῃς τὸ πάσχα;
paragraphs.translit: Kai tē prōtē hēmera tōn azymōn, hote to pascha ethyon, legousin autō hoi mathētai autou· Pou theleis apelthontes hetoimasōmen hina phagēs to pascha;

paragraphs.text: And he sendeth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ,
paragraphs.translit: kai apostellei dyo tōn mathētōn autou kai legei autois· Hypagete eis tēn polin, kai apantēsei hymin anthrōpos keramion hydatos bastazōn· akolouthēsate autō,

paragraphs.text: and wheresoever he shall enter in, say to the master of the house, The Teacher saith, Where is my guest-chamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ εἴπατε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅτι Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμά μου ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;
paragraphs.translit: kai hopou ean eiselthē eipate tō oikodespotē hoti Ho didaskalos legei· Pou estin to katalyma mou hopou to pascha meta tōn mathētōn mou phagō;

paragraphs.text: And he will himself show you a large upper room furnished [and] ready: and there make ready for us.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον ἕτοιμον· καὶ ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai autos hymin deixei anagaion mega estrōmenon hetoimon· kai ekei hetoimasate hēmin.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
paragraphs.translit: kai exēlthon hoi mathētai kai ēlthon eis tēn polin kai heuron kathōs eipen autois, kai hētoimasan to pascha.

paragraphs.text: And when it was evening he cometh with the twelve.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.
paragraphs.translit: Kai opsias genomenēs erchetai meta tōn dōdeka.

paragraphs.text: And as they sat and were eating, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you shall betray me, [even] he that eateth with me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀνακειμένων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσθιόντων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με ὁ ἐσθίων μετʼ ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai anakeimenōn autōn kai esthiontōn ho Iēsous eipen· Amēn legō hymin hoti heis ex hymōn paradōsei me ho esthiōn metʼ emou.

paragraphs.text: They began to be sorrowful, and to say unto him one by one, Is it I?
paragraphs.original: ἤρξαντο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς κατὰ εἷς· Μήτι ἐγώ;
paragraphs.translit: ērxanto lypeisthai kai legein autō heis kata heis· Mēti egō;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, [It is] one of the twelve, he that dippeth with me in the dish.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ ἐμβαπτόμενος μετʼ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὸ τρύβλιον·
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Heis tōn dōdeka, ho embaptomenos metʼ emou eis to tryblion·

paragraphs.text: For the Son of man goeth, even as it is written of him: but woe unto that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had not been born.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ διʼ οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ho men hyios tou anthrōpou hypagei kathōs gegraptai peri autou, ouai de tō anthrōpō ekeinō diʼ hou ho hyios tou anthrōpou paradidotai· kalon autō ei ouk egennēthē ho anthrōpos ekeinos.

paragraphs.text: And as they were eating, he took bread, and when he had blessed, he brake it, and gave to them, and said, Take ye: this is my body.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν· Λάβετε, τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.
paragraphs.translit: Kai esthiontōn autōn labōn arton eulogēsas eklasen kai edōken autois kai eipen· Labete, touto estin to sōma mou.

paragraphs.text: And he took a cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them: and they all drank of it.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπιον ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες.
paragraphs.translit: kai labōn potērion eucharistēsas edōken autois, kai epion ex autou pantes.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ ἐκχυννόμενον ὑπὲρ πολλῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois· Touto estin to haima mou tēs diathēkēs to ekchynnomenon hyper pollōn.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, I shall no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἐκ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti ouketi ou mē piō ek tou genēmatos tēs ampelou heōs tēs hēmeras ekeinēs hotan auto pinō kainon en tē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out unto the mount of Olives.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hymnēsantes exēlthon eis to Oros tōn Elaiōn.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus saith unto them, All ye shall be offended: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered abroad.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πάντες σκανδαλισθήσεσθε, ὅτι γέγραπται· Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα διασκορπισθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: Kai legei autois ho Iēsous hoti Pantes skandalisthēsesthe, hoti gegraptai· Pataxō ton poimena, kai ta probata diaskorpisthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: Howbeit, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
paragraphs.translit: alla meta to egerthēnai me proaxō hymas eis tēn Galilaian.

paragraphs.text: But Peter said unto him, Although all shall be offended, yet will not I.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἔφη αὐτῷ· Εἰ καὶ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται, ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐγώ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Petros ephē autō· Ei kai pantes skandalisthēsontai, allʼ ouk egō.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus saith unto him, Verily I say unto thee, that thou to-day, [even] this night, before the cock crow twice, shalt deny me thrice.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι σὺ σήμερον ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἢ δὶς ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autō ho Iēsous· Amēn legō soi hoti sy sēmeron tautē tē nykti prin ē dis alektora phōnēsai tris me aparnēsē.

paragraphs.text: But he spake exceedingly vehemently, If I must die with thee, I will not deny thee. And in like manner also said they all.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐκπερισσῶς ἐλάλει· Ἐὰν δέῃ με συναποθανεῖν σοι, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι. ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ πάντες ἔλεγον.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ekperissōs elalei· Ean deē me synapothanein soi, ou mē se aparnēsomai. hōsautōs de kai pantes elegon.

paragraphs.text: And they come unto a place which was named Gethsemane: and he saith unto his disciples, Sit ye here, while I pray.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς χωρίον οὗ τὸ ὄνομα Γεθσημανί, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Καθίσατε ὧδε ἕως προσεύξωμαι.
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchontai eis chōrion hou to onoma Gethsēmani, kai legei tois mathētais autou· Kathisate hōde heōs proseuxōmai.

paragraphs.text: And he taketh with him Peter and James and John, and began to be greatly amazed, and sore troubled.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραλαμβάνει τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην μετʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤρξατο ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν,
paragraphs.translit: kai paralambanei ton Petron kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn metʼ autou, kai ērxato ekthambeisthai kai adēmonein,

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful even unto death: abide ye here, and watch.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Perilypos estin hē psychē mou heōs thanatou· meinate hōde kai grēgoreite.

paragraphs.text: And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπιπτεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ προσηύχετο ἵνα εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν παρέλθῃ ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ ἡ ὥρα,
paragraphs.translit: kai proelthōn mikron epipten epi tēs gēs, kai prosēucheto hina ei dynaton estin parelthē apʼ autou hē hōra,

paragraphs.text: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; remove this cup from me: howbeit not what I will, but what thou wilt.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ, πάντα δυνατά σοι· παρένεγκε τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ· ἀλλʼ οὐ τί ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλὰ τί σύ.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen· Abba ho patēr, panta dynata soi· parenenke to potērion touto apʼ emou· allʼ ou ti egō thelō alla ti sy.

paragraphs.text: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith unto Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldest thou not watch one hour?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔρχεται καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Σίμων, καθεύδεις; οὐκ ἴσχυσας μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι;
paragraphs.translit: kai erchetai kai heuriskei autous katheudontas, kai legei tō Petrō· Simōn, katheudeis; ouk ischysas mian hōran grēgorēsai;

paragraphs.text: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
paragraphs.original: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ ἔλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.
paragraphs.translit: grēgoreite kai proseuchesthe, hina mē elthēte eis peirasmon· to men pneuma prothymon hē de sarx asthenēs.

paragraphs.text: And again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπών.
paragraphs.translit: kai palin apelthōn prosēuxato ton auton logon eipōn.

paragraphs.text: And again he came, and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they knew not what to answer him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάλιν ἐλθὼν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καταβαρυνόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τί ἀποκριθῶσιν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai palin elthōn heuren autous katheudontas, ēsan gar autōn hoi ophthalmoi katabarynomenoi, kai ouk ēdeisan ti apokrithōsin autō.

paragraphs.text: And he cometh the third time, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough; the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔρχεται τὸ τρίτον καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἀπέχει· ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα, ἰδοὺ παραδίδοται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai erchetai to triton kai legei autois· Katheudete to loipon kai anapauesthe· apechei· ēlthen hē hōra, idou paradidotai ho hyios tou anthrōpou eis tas cheiras tōn hamartōlōn.

paragraphs.text: Arise, let us be going: behold, he that betrayeth me is at hand.
paragraphs.original: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ὁ παραδιδούς με ἤγγικεν.
paragraphs.translit: egeiresthe agōmen· idou ho paradidous me ēngiken.

paragraphs.text: And straightway, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος παραγίνεται Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων.
paragraphs.translit: Kai euthys eti autou lalountos paraginetai Ioudas heis tōn dōdeka kai metʼ autou ochlos meta machairōn kai xylōn para tōn archiereōn kai tōn grammateōn kai tōn presbyterōn.

paragraphs.text: Now he that betrayed him had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he; take him, and lead him away safely.
paragraphs.original: δεδώκει δὲ ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν σύσσημον αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπάγετε ἀσφαλῶς.
paragraphs.translit: dedōkei de ho paradidous auton syssēmon autois legōn· Hon an philēsō autos estin· kratēsate auton kai apagete asphalōs.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come, straightway he came to him, and saith, Rabbi; and kissed him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εὐθὺς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ λέγει· Ῥαββί, καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthōn euthys proselthōn autō legei· Rhabbi, kai katephilēsen auton.

paragraphs.text: And they laid hands on him, and took him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπέβαλαν τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de epebalan tas cheiras autō kai ekratēsan auton.

paragraphs.text: But a certain one of them that stood by drew his sword, and smote the servant of the high priest, and struck off his ear.
paragraphs.original: εἷς δέ τις τῶν παρεστηκότων σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἔπαισεν τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτάριον.
paragraphs.translit: heis de tis tōn parestēkotōn spasamenos tēn machairan epaisen ton doulon tou archiereōs kai apheilen autou to ōtarion.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Are ye come out, as against a robber, with swords and staves to seize me?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με;
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho Iēsous eipen autois· Hōs epi lēstēn exēlthate meta machairōn kai xylōn syllabein me;

paragraphs.text: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but [this is done] that the scriptures might be fulfilled.
paragraphs.original: καθʼ ἡμέραν ἤμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με· ἀλλʼ ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαί.
paragraphs.translit: kathʼ hēmeran ēmēn pros hymas en tō hierō didaskōn kai ouk ekratēsate me· allʼ hina plērōthōsin hai graphai.

paragraphs.text: And they all left him, and fled.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον πάντες.
paragraphs.translit: kai aphentes auton ephygon pantes.

paragraphs.text: And a certain young man followed with him, having a linen cloth cast about him, over [his] naked [body]: and they lay hold on him;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ νεανίσκος τις συνηκολούθει αὐτῷ περιβεβλημένος σινδόνα ἐπὶ γυμνοῦ, καὶ κρατοῦσιν αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: Kai neaniskos tis synēkolouthei autō peribeblēmenos sindona epi gymnou, kai kratousin auton,

paragraphs.text: but he left the linen cloth, and fled naked.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ καταλιπὼν τὴν σινδόνα γυμνὸς ἔφυγεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de katalipōn tēn sindona gymnos ephygen.

paragraphs.text: And they led Jesus away to the high priest: and there come together with him all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀπήγαγον τὸν Ἰησοῦν πρὸς τὸν ἀρχιερέα, καὶ συνέρχονται πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai apēgagon ton Iēsoun pros ton archierea, kai synerchontai pantes hoi archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi kai hoi grammateis.

paragraphs.text: And Peter had followed him afar off, even within, into the court of the high priest; and he was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light [of the fire].
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ἕως ἔσω εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἦν συγκαθήμενος μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν καὶ θερμαινόμενος πρὸς τὸ φῶς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Petros apo makrothen ēkolouthēsen autō heōs esō eis tēn aulēn tou archiereōs kai ēn synkathēmenos meta tōn hypēretōn kai thermainomenos pros to phōs.

paragraphs.text: Now the chief priests and the whole council sought witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found it not.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον ἐζήτουν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαρτυρίαν εἰς τὸ θανατῶσαι αὐτόν, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de archiereis kai holon to synedrion ezētoun kata tou Iēsou martyrian eis to thanatōsai auton, kai ouch hēuriskon·

paragraphs.text: For many bare false witness against him, and their witness agreed not together.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἴσαι αἱ μαρτυρίαι οὐκ ἦσαν.
paragraphs.translit: polloi gar epseudomartyroun katʼ autou, kai isai hai martyriai ouk ēsan.

paragraphs.text: And there stood up certain, and bare false witness against him, saying,
paragraphs.original: καί τινες ἀναστάντες ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατʼ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες
paragraphs.translit: kai tines anastantes epseudomartyroun katʼ autou legontes

paragraphs.text: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἐγὼ καταλύσω τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον τὸν χειροποίητον καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἄλλον ἀχειροποίητον οἰκοδομήσω·
paragraphs.translit: hoti Hēmeis ēkousamen autou legontos hoti Egō katalysō ton naon touton ton cheiropoiēton kai dia triōn hēmerōn allon acheiropoiēton oikodomēsō·

paragraphs.text: And not even so did their witness agree together.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐδὲ οὕτως ἴση ἦν ἡ μαρτυρία αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai oude houtōs isē ēn hē martyria autōn.

paragraphs.text: And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς μέσον ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν λέγων· Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν; τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai anastas ho archiereus eis meson epērōtēsen ton Iēsoun legōn· Ouk apokrinē ouden; ti houtoi sou katamartyrousin;

paragraphs.text: But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and saith unto him, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐσιώπα καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίνατο οὐδέν. πάλιν ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ εὐλογητοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ho de esiōpa kai ouk apekrinato ouden. palin ho archiereus epērōta auton kai legei autō· Sy ei ho christos ho hyios tou eulogētou;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν καθήμενον τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen· Egō eimi, kai opsesthe ton hyion tou anthrōpou ek dexiōn kathēmenon tēs dynameōs kai erchomenon meta tōn nephelōn tou ouranou.

paragraphs.text: And the high priest rent his clothes, and saith, What further need have we of witnesses?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς διαρρήξας τοὺς χιτῶνας αὐτοῦ λέγει· Τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων;
paragraphs.translit: ho de archiereus diarrēxas tous chitōnas autou legei· Ti eti chreian echomen martyrōn;

paragraphs.text: Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be worthy of death.
paragraphs.original: ἠκούσατε τῆς βλασφημίας· τί ὑμῖν φαίνεται; οἱ δὲ πάντες κατέκριναν αὐτὸν ἔνοχον εἶναι θανάτου.
paragraphs.translit: ēkousate tēs blasphēmias· ti hymin phainetai; hoi de pantes katekrinan auton enochon einai thanatou.

paragraphs.text: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, Prophesy: and the officers received him with blows of their hands.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤρξαντό τινες ἐμπτύειν αὐτῷ καὶ περικαλύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ κολαφίζειν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ· Προφήτευσον, καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ῥαπίσμασιν αὐτὸν ἔλαβον.
paragraphs.translit: kai ērxanto tines emptyein autō kai perikalyptein autou to prosōpon kai kolaphizein auton kai legein autō· Prophēteuson, kai hoi hypēretai rhapismasin auton elabon.

paragraphs.text: And as Peter was beneath in the court, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὄντος τοῦ Πέτρου κάτω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ ἔρχεται μία τῶν παιδισκῶν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως,
paragraphs.translit: Kai ontos tou Petrou katō en tē aulē erchetai mia tōn paidiskōn tou archiereōs,

paragraphs.text: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and saith, Thou also wast with the Nazarene, [even] Jesus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον θερμαινόμενον ἐμβλέψασα αὐτῷ λέγει· Καὶ σὺ μετὰ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ ἦσθα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai idousa ton Petron thermainomenon emblepsasa autō legei· Kai sy meta tou Nazarēnou ēstha tou Iēsou·

paragraphs.text: But he denied, saying, I neither know, nor understand what thou sayest: and he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο λέγων· Οὔτε οἶδα οὔτε ἐπίσταμαι σὺ τί λέγεις, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω εἰς τὸ προαύλιον καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ērnēsato legōn· Oute oida oute epistamai sy ti legeis, kai exēlthen exō eis to proaulion kai alektōr ephōnēsen.

paragraphs.text: And the maid saw him, and began again to say to them that stood by, This is [one] of them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἡ παιδίσκη ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἤρξατο πάλιν λέγειν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν ὅτι Οὗτος ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hē paidiskē idousa auton ērxato palin legein tois parestōsin hoti Houtos ex autōn estin.

paragraphs.text: But he again denied it. And after a little while again they that stood by said to Peter, of a truth thou art [one] of them; for thou art a Galilaean.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ πάλιν ἠρνεῖτο. καὶ μετὰ μικρὸν πάλιν οἱ παρεστῶτες ἔλεγον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖος εἶ καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὁμοιάζει·
paragraphs.translit: ho de palin ērneito. kai meta mikron palin hoi parestōtes elegon tō Petrō· Alēthōs ex autōn ei, kai gar Galilaios ei kai hē lalia sou homoiazei·

paragraphs.text: But he began to curse, and to swear, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἤρξατο ἀναθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύναι ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὃν λέγετε.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ērxato anathematizein kai omnynai hoti Ouk oida ton anthrōpon touton hon legete.

paragraphs.text: And straightway the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word, how that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ δευτέρου ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν· καὶ ἀνεμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τὸ ῥῆμα ὡς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι δὶς τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ, καὶ ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys ek deuterou alektōr ephōnēsen· kai anemnēsthē ho Petros to rhēma hōs eipen autō ho Iēsous hoti Prin alektora phōnēsai dis tris me aparnēsē, kai epibalōn eklaien.
